newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close down after recent gains.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close down after recent gains.

text.p: Singapore shares slipped back from recent heavy gains on Monday as dealers took profits on selected blue chips.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index closed down 15.61 points at 2,178.03. Volume totalled 114.78 million shares, with 113 gainers and 235 losers.
Dealers said the fall was a correction to last week's gains.
"I think people were in the mood to take some profits after last week's strong performance," one dealer said.
"Unless there was a really compelling reason, I wouldn't be a big buyer in the market now," another said.
Topping the volume with 8.46 million shares was Hotel Properties, which fell three cents to Singapore $2.32.
Much of the activity in the stock appeared to be linked to an earlier announcement by Citibank that it had placed a 25 million call warrant issue on shares in the property developer.
Electronics distributor Thakral made strong gains of six cents to US$0.83 ahead of expected good half-year results.
Dealers said Thakral had also benefited from a buy recommendation by Fraser Securities. Thakral is due to announce its six-month results on Tuesday afternoon.
